_about: The shipped defaults for learning.json: the documented fallback for any bad or missing value there. Keep the two equal (scripts/test_learning_config.py checks). Every pattern is a case-insensitive regex fragment.

tool_failure._about: A tool result meaning the call did not do what was asked. Tools report failure in prose, and a bare 'error' anywhere would also match a news headline, so starts_with is matched at the start of the result and contains anywhere in it.
contains: is not recognized as an internal or external command

admits_failure._about: Whole words in a reply that own up to a failure. If the tools failed and the reply says one of these, she handled it honestly and the turn isn't held against her.

correction._about: His next message telling her the last reply was wrong. Matched at the start, after any number of lead_ins (each optionally followed by , ! or .): 'no' inside a sentence ('no rush') is not a correction. Widened on 2026-10-30 to how he actually says it; every complaint brain.py reruns (_COMPLAINT) must also count here (scripts/test_feedback.py checks).

praise._about: Approval of the reply, not agreement to her question: 'yes please' and a bare 'okay' answer an offer and stay unknown. Matched at the start, after at most one lead_in (optionally followed by , ! or .).

claims_done._about: A reply saying something was DONE. brain.py uses the same pattern live, to send her back before a false 'done' reaches him; here it labels the ones that got through. Any fragment matching anywhere counts.

report._about: The nightly eval report's section: how many failing prompts it lists (the command line lists cli_limit), and how much of each prompt it quotes.
